3 min read
Just now

--

We got the answers instantly, but we lost the ability to think for ourselves.
I was working on a client article last month.
Deadline was tight. So I did what everyone does now.
I opened ChatGPT, typed my prompt, and copied the answer.
10 minutes later the draft was "done".
But something felt wrong. I couldn't explain it in my own words. I didn't remember what I wrote.
That’s when it hit me.
AI didn’t make me faster. It made me forget how to think.
*The Lie We All Believe*
We were told AI would make us smarter.
Like having a genius assistant in your pocket 24/7.
And in some ways it did.
A student in Lahore can now explain calculus in Urdu.
A freelancer in Karachi can write a proposal that sounds like it came from New York.
A mom in Texas can plan meals for a week in 30 seconds.
AI removed the hard part. The thinking part.
But here’s the problem no one talks about:
*When you skip the hard part every single day, your brain stops doing it.*
*3 Ways AI Is Making Us Lazy Without Us Noticing*
*1. We stopped remembering*
Before AI, if I forgot a fact I’d Google it, read 2-3 articles, and the info would stick.
Now I ask AI once and forget it 5 minutes later.
Why remember when you can just ask again?
In Pakistan, students use AI to do assignments. In the US, employees use it to write emails.
Different countries, same result: we outsource our memory.
*2. We stopped struggling*
Struggle is where learning happens.
Writing a bad first draft teaches you more than reading a perfect AI draft.
Solving a bug for 2 hours makes you a better coder than copying the AI fix.
But AI gives us the answer before the struggle starts.
So we never build the muscle.
*3. We stopped having opinions*
Ask AI "what do you think about remote work?" and you’ll get 5 balanced bullet points.
No edge. No story. No "I".
We’re starting to talk like AI too. Safe. Generic. Robotic.
I caught myself doing this in a team meeting. Someone asked my opinion and I gave them a ChatGPT answer.
*The Mistake I Made*
My biggest mistake was treating AI like a replacement, not a tool.
I thought: "AI can write, so I don’t need to."
The right way is: "AI can write a draft, so I can spend my time making it better, more human, more me."
Think of it like this:
In the US people use calculators but still learn math.
In Pakistan people use EasyPaisa but still learn to budget.
AI should be the same. A tool, not a crutch.
*How To Use AI Without Getting Dumber*
I’m not saying quit AI. That’s not realistic.
Here’s what’s working for me in 2026:
*1. The 10-Minute Rule*
Before asking AI anything, try to solve it yourself for 10 minutes.
Write the bad draft. Solve half the problem. Then use AI to improve it.
That 10 minutes is where the growth happens.
*2. Ask "Why" not just "What"*
Don’t say "write me 3 Instagram captions".
Say "explain why these 3 captions work and how I can write my own next time".
Force AI to teach you, not do it for you.
*3. Keep one skill AI-free*
Pick one thing you will never use AI for.
For me it’s journaling. For you it could be brainstorming, coding, or talking to clients.
Keep that muscle alive.
*Final Thought*
AI is not the problem. Our relationship with it is.
The truth is: AI won’t make you lazy.
Using AI to avoid thinking will.
In 2026 the people who win won’t be the ones who use AI the most.
They’ll be the ones who use AI, and still know how to think without it.
Don’t let the tool become the brain.
What’s one skill you’ll keep AI-free this year? Drop it in the comments. I’m curious.
